site_ui.lead: Practitioners show how to decide between assigning and double closing, price transactional funding at 1% to 3% of purchase or a flat $850 to $2,000, and wire nothing on the A leg until the end buyer's cash is sitting in escrow.
site_ui.summary: All 12 chapters synthesize 192 verbatim YouTube practitioner testimonies on double closes, transactional funding, title and escrow, earnest money, and lending. Every claim, metric, pro-tip and operator gate carries timestamped inline attribution to the practitioner and video it came from.

Transactional Funding Costs, Terms & Lender Selection

Proof of Funds, Prorations & Wire Fraud
flow: Contract the A-to-B purchase, bake fees into the price at the table ($97,000 instead of $100,000), and screen bank-owned and short sale deals for 30, 60 or 90-day resale restrictions.
Sign the B-to-C contract first and secure a $2,500 minimum non-refundable deposit, $5,000 to $10,000 preferred, backed by a release clause.
Write an investor-friendly title company or attorney into both contracts, confirm they actually do double escrows, and lock their wire instructions on the first call.
Assign by default; double close when the spread crosses roughly $10,000 to $20,000 or when REO, HUD or no-assignment paper blocks an assignment.
Send both contracts to a transactional funder priced at 1% to 3% of purchase, flat $850 to $2,000, or 1% plus $100, and budget for fees if closing slips.
Fund the A leg only after the end buyer's B-to-C funds land in escrow, then repay the funder from the second closing, often within an hour.
